data.title: Don't Ignore The Insider Selling In TrueBlue
data.description:

(NYSE:TBI) should probably be aware that the Executive VP & General Counsel, Garrett Ferencz, recently divested US$170k worth of shares in the company, at an average price of US$11.96 each. However, the silver lining is that the sale only reduced their total holding by 6.1%, so we're hesitant to read anything much into it, on its own.

The Last 12 Months Of Insider Transactions At TrueBlue

Notably, that recent sale by Garrett Ferencz is the biggest insider sale of TrueBlue shares that we've seen in the last year. That means that an insider was selling shares at below the current price (US$12.41). When an insider sells below the current price, it suggests that they considered that lower price to be fair. That makes us wonder what they think of the (higher) recent valuation. However, while insider selling is sometimes discouraging, it's only a weak signal. It is worth noting that this sale was only 6.1% of Garrett Ferencz's holding.

Over the last year, we can see that insiders have bought 39.90k shares worth US$149k. But they sold 16.40k shares for US$185k. An insider hasn't bought TrueBlue stock in the last three months, but there was some selling. Despite some insider buying, the longer term picture doesn't make us feel much more positive. data.title: We're Hopeful That IZEA Worldwide (NASDAQ:IZEA) Will Use Its Cash Wisely
data.description:
There's no doubt that money can be made by owning shares of unprofitable businesses. For example, biotech and mining exploration companies often lose money for years before finding success with a new treatment or mineral discovery. But while the successes are well known, investors should not ignore the very many unprofitable companies that simply burn through all their cash and collapse.

So should IZEA Worldwide (NASDAQ:IZEA) shareholders be worried about its cash burn? For the purposes of this article, cash burn is the annual rate at which an unprofitable company spends cash to fund its growth; its negative free cash flow. First, we'll determine its cash runway by comparing its cash burn with its cash reserves.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

When Might IZEA Worldwide Run Out Of Money?

A company's cash runway is the amount of time it would take to burn through its cash reserves at its current cash burn rate. As at June 2026, IZEA Worldwide had cash of US$47m and no debt. In the last year, its cash burn was US$2.6m. That means it had a cash runway of very many years as of June 2026. Even though this is but one measure of the company's cash burn, the thought of such a long cash runway warms our bellies in a comforting way. The image below shows how its cash balance has been changing over the last few years.

See our latest analysis for IZEA Worldwide

How Well Is IZEA Worldwide Growing?

Notably, IZEA Worldwide actually ramped up its cash burn very hard and fast in the last year, by 127%, signifying heavy investment in the business. While that's concerning on it's own, the fact that operating revenue was actually down 27% over the same period makes us positively tremulous. In light of the above-mentioned, we're pretty wary of the trajectory the company seems to be on. In reality, this article only makes a short study of the company's growth data. You can take a look at how IZEA Worldwide has developed its business over time by checking this visualization of its revenue and earnings history.

How Hard Would It Be For IZEA Worldwide To Raise More Cash For Growth?

While IZEA Worldwide seems to be in a fairly good position, it's still worth considering how easily it could raise more cash, even just to fuel faster growth. Companies can raise capital through either debt or equity. Commonly, a business will sell new shares in itself to raise cash and drive growth. We can compare a company's cash burn to its market capitalisation to get a sense for how many new shares a company would have to issue to fund one year's operations.

IZEA Worldwide's cash burn of US$2.6m is about 6.8% of its US$38m market capitalisation. That's a low proportion, so we figure the company would be able to raise more cash to fund growth, with a little dilution, or even to simply borrow some money.

So, Should We Worry About IZEA Worldwide's Cash Burn?

On this analysis of IZEA Worldwide's cash burn, we think its cash runway was reassuring, while its increasing cash burn has us a bit worried. While we're the kind of investors who are always a bit concerned about the risks involved with cash burning companies, the metrics we have discussed in this article leave us relatively comfortable about IZEA Worldwide's situation. On another note, IZEA Worldwide has 2 warning signs (and 1 which is concerning) we think you should know about.

data.title: What Cloudflare Holders Bought Into
data.description:
If Cloudflare sat on your watchlist instead of in your brokerage account, the rebound might feel expensive in hindsight. Holding Cloudflare from the start of the year would have returned 56.0%, including dividends. That outcome raises a sharper question. If you had focused on one simple assumption at the start of 2026, that rising cloud-native security demand could sustain rapid revenue expansion despite competition and regulation, would Cloudflare’s potential have looked different?

The useful thing about a Narrative is that the reasoning is checkable: the assumptions sit beside the argument, and together they imply an estimated Fair Value you can disagree with.

The move put Cloudflare in the middle of this trade. Scan 53 AI infrastructure stocks for other companies exposed to it.

The Two Cloudflare Stories Investors Had To Weigh

Cloudflare shares cost US$197 at the start of the period, and you had to decide which story about the next few years felt more realistic.

The bullish Narrative saw Fair Value at US$209 and treated 26.5% revenue growth with a 4.6% profit margin as achievable, helped by demand for zero trust security and cloud-native infrastructure.

The bearish view pinned Fair Value at US$116 and accepted 24.8% revenue growth assumptions but focused on rising regulatory costs and hyperscaler competition as risks to future margins.

What The Results Changed For The Cloudflare Narrative

Cloudflare’s Q3 2026 report showed revenue of US$782.5 million compared with US$562.0 million in Q3 2025, which supported the growth side of the bullish story. Net income moved in the opposite direction, as the business reported a larger loss of US$34.1 million and net margin declined from -0.2% to -4.4%. The evidence pointed both to strong growth and weaker profitability, leaving profitability targets unproven.

The key assumption here was straightforward: strong demand was expected to translate into improving margins, not just higher sales. When you look at another high growth stock, check whether rising revenue is showing up in net income and net margin, or only in the top line.

What Cloudflare’s Run Now Assumes

Cloudflare shares now trade at US$306 from the start of the year, and this selected Narrative’s Fair Value sits below that level rather than above it. According to DaneDruss, a Simply Wall St Community investor who wrote the Narrative, the key question is how much of the security story is already baked into that price.

A buyer today would be banking on strong long term revenue growth and cleaner margins, then weighing that against the risk that post quantum security becomes expected table stakes rather than a powerful separate profit driver.

"Cloudflare is not a quantum computer company. That is the point. If Q-Day risk is moving closer, the migration layer may matter as much as the companies trying to build quantum computers."

That disagreement has a full argument behind it. → Uncover the lower Fair Value this Narrative argues for

Another Cloudflare Angle To Watch

Cloudflare highlights shifting demand for internet traffic protection and security-focused infrastructure. It also shapes how investors picture where workloads operate.

Step sideways and another challenge appears. Those applications still need a place to run, be managed and billed reliably.

An unnamed heavyweight cloud provider concentrates on a broader software and infrastructure stack. It hosts workloads, sells subscriptions and charges extra for tools like AI assistants.

That blend of seats plus usage creates a distinct exposure profile for investors. As customers stack more intensive activity on the same platform, pricing dynamics might subtly evolve.

data.title: Is It Smart To Buy BWX Technologies, Inc. (NYSE:BWXT) Before It Goes Ex-Dividend?
data.description:
Some investors rely on dividends for growing their wealth, and if you're one of those dividend sleuths, you might be intrigued to know that BWX Technologies, Inc. (NYSE:BWXT) is about to go ex-dividend in just four days. The ex-dividend date is one business day before the record date, which is the cut-off date for shareholders to be present on the company's books to be eligible for a dividend payment. It is important to be aware of the ex-dividend date because any trade on the stock needs to have been settled on or before the record date. Meaning, you will need to purchase BWX Technologies' shares before the 19th of November to receive the dividend, which will be paid on the 10th of December.

The company's next dividend payment will be US$0.27 per share, and in the last 12 months, the company paid a total of US$1.08 per share. Based on the last year's worth of payments, BWX Technologies has a trailing yield of 0.9% on the current stock price of US$122.97. If you buy this business for its dividend, you should have an idea of whether BWX Technologies's dividend is reliable and sustainable. We need to see whether the dividend is covered by earnings and if it's growing.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

Dividends are typically paid out of company income, so if a company pays out more than it earned, its dividend is usually at a higher risk of being cut. That's why it's good to see BWX Technologies paying out a modest 26% of its earnings. Yet cash flow is typically more important than profit for assessing dividend sustainability, so we should always check if the company generated enough cash to afford its dividend. It distributed 26% of its free cash flow as dividends, a comfortable payout level for most companies.

It's encouraging to see that the dividend is covered by both profit and cash flow. This generally suggests the dividend is sustainable, as long as earnings don't drop precipitously.

Have Earnings And Dividends Been Growing?

Stocks in companies that generate sustainable earnings growth often make the best dividend prospects, as it is easier to lift the dividend when earnings are rising. If earnings decline and the company is forced to cut its dividend, investors could watch the value of their investment go up in smoke. With that in mind, we're encouraged by the steady growth at BWX Technologies, with earnings per share up 7.0% on average over the last five years. The company is retaining more than half of its earnings within the business, and it has been growing earnings at a decent rate. We think this is generally an attractive combination, as dividends can grow through a combination of earnings growth and or a higher payout ratio over time.

The main way most investors will assess a company's dividend prospects is by checking the historical rate of dividend growth. In the last 10 years, BWX Technologies has lifted its dividend by approximately 12% a year on average. It's encouraging to see the company lifting dividends while earnings are growing, suggesting at least some corporate interest in rewarding shareholders.

Final Takeaway

Is BWX Technologies an attractive dividend stock, or better left on the shelf? Earnings per share have been growing moderately, and BWX Technologies is paying out less than half its earnings and cash flow as dividends, which is an attractive combination as it suggests the company is investing in growth. It might be nice to see earnings growing faster, but BWX Technologies is being conservative with its dividend payouts and could still perform reasonably over the long run. Northrop Grumman shares have climbed 69.0% over the past 5 years, which puts fresh focus on a simple question for you as an investor. Is the current US$550.43 price supported by the cash the business is expected to generate over time, based on a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) view of the stock?

  • The 69.0% gain over 5 years raises the stakes on whether that long stretch of returns lines up with the value implied by Northrop Grumman's future cash flows.
  • Recent contract outcomes, including missing out on the F/A-XX fighter program while gaining C-130 depot work, can shift expectations for long term defense cash flow, program mix and capital needs across the portfolio.
  • What if you looked at Northrop Grumman through its earnings instead? See why Northrop Grumman's 17.3x P/E tells a different valuation story.

The issue now is whether the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) view of Northrop Grumman's business supports paying today's market price for its shares.

If you are weighing Northrop Grumman through its cash flows and contract wins and losses, it can help to set it alongside other defense focused names using 31 resilient stocks with low risk scores.

Is Northrop Grumman Fairly Priced on Cash Flow?

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) approach here focuses on the cash Northrop Grumman can return to shareholders over time. Over the last twelve months, the group produced roughly $3.6b of free cash flow, and the model assumes those cash flows grow steadily rather than swinging sharply up or down. Longer term, the projections extend this pattern into the next decade, with estimates that stay in the multi billion dollar range each year.

Those assumptions lead to an estimated intrinsic value that sits broadly in line with the current US$550.43 share price. Northrop Grumman declining to protest its loss of the F/A-XX program sits alongside the win of C-130 depot work, and that mix of contract outcomes may help explain why the market currently values the stock close to what the DCF suggests. The Northrop Grumman Narrative: What Would Justify Today's Price?

Simply Wall St Narratives pick up where the Northrop Grumman valuation puzzle leaves off and explain what kind of future growth, margins and earnings profile would need to occur for the stock to appear meaningfully higher or lower than today’s price, all housed on the Community page. Each Narrative links its number to a clear view on how Northrop Grumman's growth path, profitability and risk profile could change over time, so you can revisit the logic as fresh information becomes available.

The two Northrop Grumman Narratives look at the same backlog and guidance, yet they disagree on how much of that story the current price already reflects.

Bull case: 13% undervalued

This view comes from the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St, which pulls together mainstream forecasts and targets.

"Analysts expect Northrop Grumman to benefit from rising U.S. and allied defense spending, a record $105 billion backlog, and growth in national security space and key production programs…"

Discover why this Narrative puts Northrop Grumman at 13% undervalued.

Bear case: 17% overvalued

This angle is set out in the bearish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St, which leans on the most cautious targets and assumptions.

"Bearish analysts expect Northrop Grumman to face ongoing margin pressure in Defense Systems and Space Systems as qualification and redesign costs on programs like SiAW and GEM 63XL weigh on profitability…"

data.title: Biodesix Independent Director Acquires 4.2% More Stock
data.description:
Those following along with Biodesix, Inc. (NASDAQ:BDSX) will no doubt be intrigued by the recent purchase of shares by Jack Schuler, Independent Director of the company, who spent a stonking US$1.0m on stock at an average price of US$10.02. There's no denying a buy of that magnitude suggests conviction in a brighter future, although we do note that proportionally it only increased their holding by 4.2%.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Biodesix Insider Transactions Over The Last Year

In fact, the recent purchase by Independent Director Jack Schuler was not their only acquisition of Biodesix shares this year. They previously made an even bigger purchase of US$1.2m worth of shares at a price of US$11.81 per share. That means that an insider was happy to buy shares at above the current price of US$9.88. It's very possible they regret the purchase, but it's more likely they are bullish about the company. To us, it's very important to consider the price insiders pay for shares. It is encouraging to see an insider paid above the current price for shares, as it suggests they saw value, even at higher levels. Jack Schuler was the only individual insider to buy during the last year.

Jack Schuler bought a total of 325.07k shares over the year at an average price of US$12.67. You can see a visual depiction of insider transactions (by companies and individuals) over the last 12 months, below. By clicking on the graph below, you can see the precise details of each insider transaction!

View our latest analysis for Biodesix

Biodesix is not the only stock insiders are buying. So take a peek at this free list of under-the-radar companies with insider buying.

Insider Ownership Of Biodesix

For a common shareholder, it is worth checking how many shares are held by company insiders. A high insider ownership often makes company leadership more mindful of shareholder interests. Insiders own 40% of Biodesix shares, worth about US$43m. This level of insider ownership is good but just short of being particularly stand-out. It certainly does suggest a reasonable degree of alignment.

So What Does This Data Suggest About Biodesix Insiders?

The recent insider purchase is heartening. And an analysis of the transactions over the last year also gives us confidence. But we don't feel the same about the fact the company is making losses. Given that insiders also own a fair bit of Biodesix we think they are probably pretty confident of a bright future. So these insider transactions can help us build a thesis about the stock, but it's also worthwhile knowing the risks facing this company.
